title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is chapter III of the 1986 notes 'Réseaux via découpages'. Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial theory of 'découpages', meaning ways of cutting a space into pieces, as a foundation for tame ('modérée') topology. On the previous page, Example 1 takes an ordered set L. It is filtering upward and downward, has no greatest or least element, is locally filtering in both directions and is dense ('divisible'). He calls such a set a 'ligne ordonnée' (ordered line). He sets S_0 = P_2(L), the 2-element subsets. He sets Modf(L) = finite totally ordered subsets T = {t_1 < ... < t_n}, whose complement has connected components ]-inf,t_1[, ]t_1,t_2[, ..., ]t_n,+inf[.

This page opens: 'This structure is a découpage ... the linear découpages for opposite orders, i.e. they differ only in the boundaries.' The likely meaning is that L and its opposite order give essentially the same cutting structure, differing only in boundary data.

An abandoned heading ('Positions modifiées / disjointes') is struck out. He then defines 'tronçons' (pieces) of the line: closed segments [s,t] with s <= t, closed half-lines ]-inf,s] or [s,+inf[, and the whole line L = ]-inf,+inf[. Their boundaries are {s,t}, {s} and the empty set respectively.

Two tronçons are 'in tame (modérée / modifiée) relative position' if their boundaries are. A 'position modérée' is then a finite union of mutually tame, pairwise disjoint tronçons. By disjointness its boundary is the disjoint union of the boundaries. The diagonal marginal note seems to restate this for the line case: boundary of a union of disjoint, mutually tame tronçons.

The next page abstracts the notion into an axiomatic 'tronçon ordonné'. The axioms are local filtering above and below each point, global filtering, a density-type axiom, and card > 1. These distinguish segments (with both endpoints) from intervals (with neither).

The purpose is to model the one-dimensional case (the line and its tame subsets: finitely many points and intervals) inside a general combinatorial framework of découpages and réseaux. This is the 1-dimensional base case of a tame-topology axiomatics.
errors: Degenerate case s = t: [s,s] = {s} has boundary {s}, not a 2-element set {s,t}. The stated boundary {s,t} implicitly assumes s < t; the 2-element sets S_0 = P_2(L) of the previous page suggest that is intended.

The notion of two finite boundary sets being 'in tame relative position' is used here before it is defined on this page. It presumably means something like disjointness or general position of boundaries, but is left implicit.

Disjoint closed tronçons: requiring disjointness of closed pieces means the finite unions only cover sets whose components are closed. Open or half-open pieces (needed for complements) are not yet handled. This is a gap in closure under complement that the axiomatics on later pages presumably addresses.

ideas.what: Line as a dense ordered set without endpoints; finite subsets cut it into finitely many open intervals ('découpage linéaire')
ideas.modern_name: Dense linear orders / definable sets in o-minimal structures (cell decomposition in dimension 1)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme announced only informally in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6; this découpage formalism is unpublished

ideas.what: Tronçons (closed segments, half-lines, whole line) with their endpoint boundaries; finite disjoint unions of mutually tame tronçons with boundary = disjoint union of boundaries
ideas.modern_name: Finite unions of intervals / semilinear sets in dimension 1; boundary additivity

ideas.what: Invariance of the découpage structure under passing to the opposite order (differs only by boundaries)
Axiomatic 'tronçon ordonné' (next page): local filtering conditions replacing total order
ideas.modern_name: Locally directed/dense posets as abstract 1-dimensional tame spaces

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 découpage axiomatics treats the ordered line with finitely-cut pieces and boundary bookkeeping in parallel with, and apparently independently of, the contemporaneous o-minimal programme (Pillay–Steinhorn 1986). Note the use of filtering posets rather than total orders. The link between his 'réseaux via découpages' and o-minimal cell decomposition is not documented in detail in the literature.
missed.quote: Position modifiée : réunion finie de tronçons mutuellement modifiés, et disjoints. Par disjonction, le bord est la réunion (disjointe) des bords.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would document Grothendieck's own concrete route to tame topology, which the Esquisse only sketched. It might suggest a poset-based (non-totally-ordered) generalisation of o-minimal dimension-1 theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Mathematically elementary: the definitions of intervals, half-lines and boundaries of finite unions are routine. Its interest is only as part of an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology framework from 1986.
transcription_corrections: 'modifiée(s)'/'modifiés' is probably 'modérée(s)'/'modérés' (tame), consistent with Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée'.
First line likely 'Cette structure est un découpage, [?] les découpages linéaires pour ordres opposés, i.e. elles ne diffèrent que des bords' (rather than 'par ordres').
'Tronçons de la ligne : parties de L de la forme' rather than 'qui sont[?]'.
'{+troisième+}' is an insertion: '∅ dans le troisième'.
